mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to monetary tightening, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY > 2%, or if the correlation between CPIAUCSL YoY and 20-day forward returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and increased production costs, negatively impacting corporate profit margins and thus S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE < 5%, or if the correlation between UNRATE and 60-day forward returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Real Final Sales of Domestic Product (RSAFS) signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances following RSAFS increases, or if the correlation between RSAFS and 5-day forward returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average signals a weakening supply side, which can lead to reduced corporate output and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO < 12-month MA, or if the correlation between INDPRO and 20-day forward returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is rising, the combination signals a tightening monetary policy in response to inflation, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL is rising, or if the joint effect of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on 60-day forward returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5% and Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) are increasing, the combination signals a tightening labor market with strong job growth, which can lead to wage inflation and increased production costs, negatively impacting corporate profit margins and thus S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tight labor market with job growth
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE < 5% and PAYEMS is increasing, or if the joint effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS on 20-day forward returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) signals strengthening demand in the housing market, which boosts related industries and consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances following sustained increases in HOUST, or if the correlation between HOUST and 60-day forward returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When Industrial Production (INDPRO) is above its 12-month moving average and Real GDP (GDPC1) is growing, the combination signals a strong supply side and economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO > 12-month MA and GDPC1 is growing, or if the joint effect of INDPRO and GDPC1 on 20-day forward returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).
